question: What is the primary focus of modern occupational health nursing?

options.B: Promoting and maintaining worker health and safety
options.C: Treating severe chronic illnesses in community clinics
options.D: Conducting bedside nursing care in surgical wards

explanation: Occupational health nursing specifically targets the health, safety, and well-being of workers in relation to their working environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h1)

question: How has the role of the occupational health nurse shifted compared to historical industrial nursing?

options.A: From administrative desk tasks to exclusive surgical assistance
options.B: From reactive injury treatment to proactive risk prevention
options.C: From factory floor management to hospital emergency triage
options.D: From public health advocacy to private domestic caregiving

explanation: Early industrial nursing focused mostly on treating workplace injuries after they happened, whereas contemporary practice emphasizes hazard identification and prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h1)

question: Which task is a core responsibility of an occupational health nurse during injury recovery?

options.A: Liquidating company assets to cover medical bills
options.B: Coordinating return-to-work plans for injured employees
options.C: Prescribing permanent disability pensions without review
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries on the factory floor

explanation: Case management, including structured return-to-work planning, is a primary duty when handling employee injuries and rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h2)

question: A practitioner who evaluates a workstation layout to prevent repetitive strain injuries is acting primarily as what?

options.A: An environmental and ergonomic risk evaluator
options.C: A hospital emergency room admissions clerk

explanation: Assessing workstation setups to prevent musculoskeletal strain falls squarely under workplace risk assessment and ergonomics. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary legislative act governing factory safety and worker welfare in Nigeria?
explanation: The Factories Act is the principal legislation in Nigeria that mandates safety, health, and welfare requirements in industrial workplaces. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h3)

question: Why must an occupational health nurse in Nigeria be familiar with the Employee's Compensation Act?

options.A: It regulates nursing school admission criteria across universities
options.B: It outlines procedures for compensating workers with occupational injuries
options.C: It determines the national minimum wage scales for civil servants
options.D: It dictates the exact medication formulary for hospital pharmacies

explanation: The Employee's Compensation Act provides open provisions and financial support mechanisms for workers who sustain injuries or contract diseases at work. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h3)

question: Which category of workplace hazard includes exposure to loud industrial noise and extreme temperatures?
explanation: Physical hazards encompass environmental factors such as noise, vibration, radiation, and temperature extremes that can harm the body. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h4)

question: A laboratory technician handling patient blood samples is primarily exposed to which type of workplace hazard?
explanation: Pathogens, bloodborne viruses, and infectious microorganisms fall under biological hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a pre-employment medical examination?

options.A: To provide immediate emergency treatment for acute factory trauma
options.B: To establish a baseline health status and evaluate fitness for work
options.C: To diagnose chronic community illnesses unrelated to the job
options.D: To determine the final retirement pension package for the employee

explanation: Pre-employment exams provide a health baseline so that future occupational changes or injuries can be accurately measured against pre-existing conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h5)

question: Routine audiometric testing for factory workers exposed to loud machinery is an example of what practice?
explanation: Audiometric testing tracks hearing thresholds over time to detect early signs of noise-induced damage before permanent loss occurs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h5)

question: What is the immediate priority when an employee sustains an acute injury on the factory floor?

options.C: Holding a company-wide safety disciplinary meeting

explanation: Immediate medical stabilization and first aid are always the first priorities following any acute workplace injury. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h6)

question: Why is modified or light-duty work often recommended during an employee's recovery phase?

options.A: It punishes the worker for failing to follow safety guidelines
options.B: It maintains engagement and supports safe, gradual reintegration
options.C: It completely exempts the employer from paying medical insurance
options.D: It replaces the need for any formal workplace hazard assessment

explanation: Modified duties bridge the gap between full disability and full recovery, preventing prolonged absence and promoting healing. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h6)

question: What is the core principle of workplace ergonomics?

options.A: Increasing production speed regardless of human fatigue
options.B: Forcing workers to adapt to rigid machinery designs
options.C: Reducing employee health benefits to lower corporate costs
options.D: Fitting the job and equipment to the worker

explanation: Ergonomics centers on adapting workstations, tools, and tasks to match human physical capabilities and limitations. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of an ergonomic intervention?

options.A: Redesigning hand tools to reduce excessive wrist twisting
options.B: Installing adjustable-height chairs for computer operators
options.C: Providing mechanical hoists to assist with heavy material lifting
options.D: Increasing the required speed of an assembly line without rest breaks

explanation: Forcing faster speeds without rest breaks increases physical strain and violates ergonomic principles of reducing fatigue and musculoskeletal stress. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h7)

question: What term describes the ethical tension between serving corporate employer interests and advocating for employee health?
explanation: Dual loyalty refers to the conflict healthcare professionals face when their responsibilities to their employer clash with their primary duty to patients. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h8)

question: An employer demands access to an employee's confidential medical screening results. How should the occupational health nurse respond?

options.A: Destroy all medical records so no one can access them ever
options.B: Post the results on the factory notice board for complete transparency
options.C: Protect confidentiality and refuse disclosure without proper employee consent
options.D: Hand over the complete medical file immediately to satisfy management

explanation: Medical confidentiality must be maintained, and health details cannot be shared with employers without informed employee consent, except in specific statutory exceptions. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h8)
